chunks: From him, from Al-Qasim ibn Yahya, from his grandfather Al-Hasan ibn Rashid, from Yaqub ibn Ja'far ibn Ibrahim Al-Ja'fari, who said:

I heard Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him) saying: 'The one who ties up an old horse, three sins are erased from him every day and eleven good deeds are written for him; and the one who ties up a hybrid horse, two sins are erased from him every day and seven good deeds are written for him; and the one who ties up a workhorse intending by it beauty, or fulfilling needs, or repelling an enemy from him, one sin is erased from him every day and six good deeds are written for him.'
ai.seo_question: What are the daily spiritual rewards for tying different types of horses according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Recorded in Al-Kafi, this hadith details the daily spiritual accounting for maintaining cavalry horses, reflecting the pre-modern military context where 'jihad' often involved mounted warfare. It distinguishes rewards based on the horse's quality and the specific intent—whether for general readiness, aesthetic display, or practical utility—highlighting the Shia emphasis on intention (niyyah) in transforming mundane acts into worship.
